syncInfoTitle: Recording playback may show desynchronization not present in the recorded videos. Matched frame numbers represent images from the same time slice.  We are working on a fix.
syncInfoBody: Browser video playback does not guarantee sample-accurate synchronization across multiple streams. The player uses a leader-follower strategy and corrects drift when it exceeds a small tolerance, but minor desynchronization (1–2 frames) can occur
estimatedFromFrameNumber: Estimated from frame number × recording fps — not read from timestamp data
name: Name
showTranslationIndicatorDescription: Display a badge when using AI-generated translations
displayTooltipLong: Display represents the UI rendering performance. It shows how quickly your display receives and renders frames. Performance issues here won't affect recording quality but may impact your ability to monitor cameras in real-time.
serverTooltipLong: Server represents camera frame capture performance: the true rate at which frames are pulled from cameras and saved during recording. This is the key recording-quality metric and should remain stable even if display performance fluctuates.
statsSourceShort: Display renders frames, Server captures frames.
statsSourceLong: The server is the true rate at which frames are pulled/recorded from the camera, while display is the rate at which they are received and rendered. FreeMoCap prioritizes server-side performance for recording quality, so that number should stay more stable. If the display framerate diverges from the server, it indicates your system resources are taxed. Consider using fewer cameras or decreasing framerate/resolution.
statsCurrentShort: Most recent frame time and corresponding FPS.
statsCurrentLong: This shows the most recent measurement of how long it takes to process a single frame (in milliseconds) and the equivalent frames per second (FPS). Lower frame times and higher FPS indicate better performance.
statsMinShort: Fastest frame time (lowest latency) and highest FPS achieved.
statsMinLong: This represents the minimum time it took to process a single frame during the sampling window. This corresponds to the maximum FPS your system achieved during optimal conditions.
statsMaxShort: Slowest frame time (highest latency) and lowest FPS experienced.
statsMaxLong: This represents the maximum time it took to process a single frame during the sampling window. This corresponds to the minimum FPS your system achieved during worst-case conditions. Occasional spikes are normal, but consistently high values may indicate performance issues.
statsMeanShort: Average frame time and FPS across all samples.
statsMeanLong: The arithmetic mean (average) of all frame times measured during the sampling window and the corresponding FPS. This gives a good overall picture of performance but may be skewed by outliers.
statsMedianShort: Middle value of all frame times (50th percentile).
statsMedianLong: The median represents the middle value when all frame times are sorted from fastest to slowest. Unlike the mean, the median is not affected by extreme outliers, making it a more stable indicator of typical performance.
statsStdDevShort: Measures frame time variability. CV% is relative variability.
statsStdDevLong: Standard deviation measures the amount of variation in frame times. Lower values indicate more consistent performance. The Coefficient of Variation (CV%) expresses this variability as a percentage of the mean, making it easier to compare stability across different frame rates. Lower CV% indicates more stable performance.

welcome.title: Welcome to FreeMoCap
welcome.text: Let's walk the main path: connecting the local server, your cameras, the realtime pipeline, calibration, and your first recording. It only takes a minute.

tabs.title: Streaming vs Playback
tabs.text: Last thing — these two tabs up top. Streaming (where you are now) is for live cameras and recording; your captures then show up under Playback, where you review and process them.

server.title: Server connection
server.text: FreeMoCap is a client–server app: this window talks to a FreeMoCap server running locally on your own computer. This panel shows that connection — it links up automatically, and you can toggle it here to reconnect.

camera.title: Connect your cameras
camera.text: Once the server is connected, detect and connect your cameras here. Each camera has its own settings, and you can toggle whether it's included in the realtime pipeline.

realtime.title: Realtime pipeline
realtime.text: These controls run the live pipeline. Toggle 2D skeleton tracking, 3D triangulation, and filtering on or off, and choose which tracking model to use — all live as you stream.

controls.title: Turning it on & off
controls.text: The lightning toggle turns the live pipeline fully on or off (it's not a pause — pausing the cameras is what pauses the pipeline, automatically). If you turn it on while your cameras are off, it connects your selected cameras first, then starts the pipeline. With it on, switch 2D skeleton tracking, 3D triangulation, and filtering on or off, and pick the tracking model — each stage adds detail (and compute), so turn off what you don't need.

recording.title: It never slows your recording
recording.text: The realtime pipeline is designed so it can't interfere with recording. Even if the live preview can't keep up with your cameras' full frame rate, the videos saved to disk are captured at the full requested frame rate — so when you process a recording later, you get full-frame-rate data no matter how fast the live pipeline ran.

calibration.title: Calibrate your cameras
calibration.text: To get 3D motion capture from multiple cameras, calibrate them first — this works out where each camera sits in space. (A single camera works without calibration.) See the guide to calibrate with a ChArUco board.

recording.title: Record your capture
recording.text: When you're ready, hit Start Recording. Auto-process is on by default, so FreeMoCap runs motion capture automatically as soon as the recording finishes.

finish.title: You're all set!
finish.text: That's the main path — server, cameras, pipeline, calibration, and recording. Dig into the docs for more, and replay this tour any time from the Welcome screen, Settings, or the Help menu.

status.title: Connection status
status.text: The colored dot shows whether the local server is reachable, and the row below it shows the websocket — FreeMoCap is "connected" once that websocket is open.

toggle.title: Start, stop & reconnect
toggle.text: Open this panel to start or stop the local server and reconnect the websocket. It reconnects on its own, but this is where you take manual control if something gets stuck.

detect.title: Detect & connect
detect.text: Detect scans for plugged-in cameras; Connect starts streaming from the ones you've selected. Each detected camera shows up as a row you can expand.

settings.title: Per-camera settings
settings.text: Expand a camera to set its resolution, exposure and rotation, and use the toggles to include or exclude it from the capture group and the realtime pipeline.
